question: What is the primary driver behind the systemic physiological alterations observed during gestation?

options.A: A significant decrease in overall basal metabolic rate
options.B: Chronic maternal nutritional deficiencies in late gestation
options.C: Escalating hormonal signals from the placenta and corpus luteum
options.D: Direct physical compression of organs by the growing uterus

explanation: Hormones secreted by the corpus luteum and placenta act as the master regulators for nearly all systemic adjustments during gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h1)

question: Why is a thorough grasp of normal maternal physiology essential for nurses in antenatal care settings?

options.A: To accurately predict the exact delivery date without ultrasound imaging
options.B: To prevent the misdiagnosis of normal gestational variants as pathological conditions
options.C: To completely halt all natural hormonal shifts during the first trimester
options.D: To eliminate the need for routine maternal blood pressure monitoring

explanation: Many normal pregnancy changes mimic disease signs, so nurses must recognize them as healthy adaptations to avoid unnecessary anxiety or interventions. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h1)

question: What causes physiological anemia in pregnant women?

options.A: Severe bone marrow suppression caused by elevated progesterone
options.B: Plasma volume increases proportionally much more than red blood cell mass
options.C: Complete cessation of iron absorption in the small intestine
options.D: Sudden destruction of erythrocytes by placental antibodies

explanation: The blood becomes diluted because fluid volume expands significantly faster than cellular components, leading to a lower hemoglobin concentration. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h2)

question: A woman in her third trimester feels dizzy, pale, and nauseated while lying flat on her back during a clinic examination. What is the most likely physiological cause?

options.A: Acute elevation of systemic vascular resistance causing cerebral ischemia
options.B: Sudden spike in maternal red blood cell mass triggering hyperviscosity
options.C: Complete occlusion of the abdominal aorta by fetal movement
options.D: Compression of the inferior vena cava by the gravid uterus reducing venous return

explanation: Supine hypotension syndrome occurs when the heavy uterus blocks blood return to the heart, dropping cardiac output and blood pressure. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism responsible for maternal hyperventilation during gestation?

options.A: Direct physical stretching of the intercostal muscles by the ribs
options.B: Mechanical obstruction of the upper airway by soft tissue edema
options.C: Progesterone acting centrally on the brainstem to alter carbon dioxide thresholds
options.D: A compensatory response to severe primary metabolic alkalosis

explanation: Elevated progesterone sensitizes the respiratory center, causing deeper and more frequent breathing even when oxygen levels are normal. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h3)

question: Which pulmonary volume typically decreases during pregnancy due to the upward displacement of the diaphragm?
explanation: The upward push of the uterus reduces the volume of air remaining in the lungs after a normal breath, which explains why pregnant women desaturate faster during airway emergencies. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h3)

question: How does the glomerular filtration rate typically change during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It increases significantly by up to fifty percent
options.B: It fluctuates wildly depending on the time of day
options.C: It decreases steadily to conserve essential electrolytes
options.D: It remains entirely unchanged throughout all three trimesters

explanation: The kidneys work harder to clear waste products, which elevates the glomerular filtration rate early in the first trimester. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women particularly susceptible to ascending urinary tract infections?

options.A: A permanent alkaline shift in total body pH balance
options.B: Progesterone-induced ureteral dilation and urinary stasis
options.C: Reduced renal plasma flow slowing down bacterial clearance
options.D: Complete destruction of the bladder mucosa by fetal hormones

explanation: When urine flow slows down through relaxed, widened ureters, bacteria can easily multiply and ascend toward the kidneys. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h4)

question: What is the primary cause of heartburn and delayed gastric emptying in pregnant women?

options.A: Hypersecretion of hydrochloric acid by the parietal cells of the stomach
options.B: Physical blockage of the pyloric sphincter by the growing fetal head
options.C: Progesterone-induced smooth muscle relaxation throughout the digestive tract
options.D: Excessive consumption of highly spiced traditional foods

explanation: Progesterone relaxes gastrointestinal smooth muscle, slowing down food transit and allowing stomach acids to slip back into the esophagus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h5)

question: Why does the maternal body develop peripheral insulin resistance during the later stages of gestation?

options.A: To prevent the mother from storing any excess fat reserves for lactation
options.B: To accelerate maternal bone mineralization and prevent dental caries
options.C: To compensate for a sudden and dangerous drop in pancreatic insulin production
options.D: To ensure a continuous, adequate supply of glucose crosses the placenta to the fetus

explanation: By making maternal cells less responsive to insulin, more glucose remains circulating in the blood available for active fetal uptake. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h5)

question: Which hormone is responsible for maintaining the corpus luteum during the early weeks of gestation?
explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin signals the corpus luteum to continue producing progesterone until the placenta is fully functional. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h6)

question: What is a major immunological function of elevated maternal cortisol levels during pregnancy?

options.A: Suppressing maternal immune responses to prevent rejection of the fetus
options.B: Directly stimulating the fetal bone marrow to produce erythrocytes
options.C: Enhancing uterine muscle contractions in preparation for normal labor
options.D: Accelerating the breakdown of maternal red blood cells

explanation: Higher cortisol helps modulate the maternal immune system so it tolerates the genetically distinct fetal tissue as an allograft. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h6)

question: Which hormone contributes significantly to the softening of pelvic ligaments and joints during pregnancy?
explanation: Relaxin loosens pelvic connective tissue and joints to accommodate passage of the baby through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h7)

question: What is the primary mechanical reason for the development of lordosis in late pregnancy?

options.A: The forward shift in the maternal center of gravity caused by the growing uterus
options.B: Severe calcium depletion leading to softening of the vertebrae
options.C: A sudden increase in bone density throughout the axial skeleton
options.D: Spasms of the lower abdominal wall muscles caused by stretching

explanation: As the abdomen pushes forward, the mother leans back to maintain balance, creating an exaggerated inward curve in the lower spine. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h7)

question: Which set of symptoms should a nurse teach a pregnant woman to report immediately as potential warning signs of pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Severe headache, visual disturbances, and sudden facial swelling
options.B: Mild dependent ankle edema at the end of a long day
options.C: Mild heartburn relieved by simple antacids and small meals
options.D: Infrequent Braxton Hicks contractions without cervical change

explanation: Headaches, vision changes, and sudden swelling above the waist are classic red flags for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h8)

question: What practical positioning advice should a nurse give to a pregnant woman experiencing dizziness and faintness while resting in bed?

options.A: Lie strictly in a lateral side-lying position to relieve vena caval compression
options.B: Lie completely flat on the back with legs elevated above the heart
options.C: Sleep in a completely prone position with a pillow under the abdomen
options.D: Stand up quickly and walk around to stimulate venous return from the legs

explanation: Side-lying shifts the weight of the uterus off the major blood vessels, instantly restoring cardiac output and relieving dizziness. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h8)
